<mission>
Implement three compression quality fixes across structured-output.ts and snapshot.ts:

FIX 1 — Add FileEntry validation in src/structured-output.ts:

Add a new function isValidFileEntry(item: unknown): boolean that checks:
- item is a record/object
- item.path exists and is a string (REQUIRED)
- item.role is optional but if present must be a string
- item.description is optional but if present must be a string

Then update isValidStructuredOutput() to validate the files array with this per-item check. Currently it only does isOptionalArray(obj, "files"). Add: (obj.files as unknown[]).every(isValidFileEntry) when files is defined. This ensures malformed FileEntry objects are rejected upstream.

FIX 2 — Strip details from tool result messages in src/snapshot.ts:

In sanitizeForkSnapshot(), when processing message events where message.role === "tool", remove the details field from the message object. The details field contains {mode, flowStyle, projectAgentsDir, results: [...]} which is large metadata the child flow never needs. Add this alongside the existing strips for api, provider, model, etc.

FIX 3 — Compression safety net in src/snapshot.ts:

In renderCompressedFlowResult() or wherever compressed output is rendered and then used, add a quality check AFTER rendering: if the rendered output has more than 50% of its file entries filtered out as invalid (compare original files array length vs rendered file lines), OR if the rendered output contains the string "undefined", fall back to a truncated raw result instead. The truncated raw result should be: the original flow result string truncated to ~2000 chars with a "[truncated]" suffix. This ensures we NEVER pass broken compressed output to a child context.

After all changes, run npm run build to verify TypeScript compilation succeeds. Do NOT run npm test yet (that's Phase 4/step 4).

Execute this mission. Use only your available tools. If blocked, report why — do not guess.
Follow the output format specified in your directive.
</mission>
